R2073.model_description: HOMER Pro PV-battery energy simulation used for system sizing and yield
R2073.automated_input_evidence: System performance was analyzed using HOMER Pro simulation for energy modeling and Excel-based calculations for techno-economic analysis.
R2073.actuation_evidence: For example, if TDS rises above 500 ppm, the system increases the pump flow from 8 to 12 L/min.
R2073.justification: The only virtual model is an offline HOMER Pro energy simulation with no automated link to installation data. The ESP32 control of pump and voltage runs on fixed TDS/pH thresholds, and the MQTT app only shows data and sends alerts to people.

R2167.automated_input_evidence: All key system parameters, including sensor readings and power status, are displayed on an LCD screen
R2167.actuation_evidence: below a defined threshold, the system automatically
R2167.justification: This is a microcontroller project that switches irrigation when soil moisture crosses a threshold and shows sensor readings on an LCD. No model of light, energy, crop or microclimate is described.

R2468.automated_input_evidence: The LDR readings are processed by the ESP32 using a thresholdbased differential comparison method.
R2468.actuation_evidence: When the soil moisture level falls below this threshold, the ESP32 activates the relay-controlled DC water pump to provide irrigation when required.
R2468.justification: Both the servo panel tracking (LDR difference above 20 ADC units) and the irrigation (soil moisture at or below 40%) are threshold rules, and Blynk is a monitoring and manual-override dashboard. No virtual model is in the loop, so the study is NA even though a miniature prototype was tested.

R2470.model_description: none (COCO-pretrained YOLOv8 apple detector plus rule-based HSV colour index)
R2470.automated_input_evidence: Finally, the collected data were automatically transmitted via the communication module (Cortex M4 processor module) equipped with UMTS (3G) and LTE (4G) standards to a cloud-based platform
R2470.justification: Images are transmitted automatically to the cloud, but they feed only an object detector and an HSV red-pixel colour index analysed offline. Neither of these models the behaviour of the system, which matches the image-classification-only exclusion. Nothing is actuated.

R2706.automated_input_evidence: Data from sensors were collected every 30 second and were used to determine the optimal orientation of the trackers of the DAV system.
R2706.actuation_evidence: solar panels were placed in horizontal position during rain events before harvest and solar-tracking position (maximum shading for the trees) [4] when air temperature was above a given threshold.
R2706.justification: The commercial dynamic agrivoltaic trackers are steered from weather-station data by rules: horizontal during rain, solar tracking above an air-temperature threshold. The packet describes no model in the loop. The phrase 'optimal orientation' and reference [4] hint at a model, but this text does not show one.

R2710.model_description: none (only descriptive linear regression of panel temperature versus voltage)
R2710.automated_input_evidence: A database that uses structured query language (SQL) was used to store all the data that is automatically received by the central computer at regular intervals of twenty seconds.
R2710.justification: PV current, voltage and temperature are acquired automatically over ZigBee into an SQL database. They are used only for descriptive comparison and a post-hoc regression, not for a virtual model of system behaviour. There is no actuation, so this is pure data acquisition and monitoring.

R1623.model_description: Analytical solar incidence-angle model of tracking efficiency and inter-row spacing for PV designs
R1623.automated_input_evidence: The above designs were used to study the tracking efficiency of agrivoltaics systems using simulation modeling
R1623.justification: An analytical design study computes tracking efficiency from the angle of incidence on module planes for several tracker designs. No installation data or actuation is involved. It is borderline with sun-position formulas alone, but it models PV light interception and array spacing, so it is coded digital_model.

R1682.model_description: PV system design simulation and lighting/heating power-consumption estimation models
R1682.automated_input_evidence: The method for estimating the power consumption of the artificial lighting system considers the experimental measurement of luminosity and different set point values for activating the system.
R1682.actuation_evidence: The artificial lighting system is activated by the computerized intelligent system based on fuzzy logic, which makes decisions based on design premises and monitors the internal luminosity of the greenhouse.
R1682.justification: The greenhouses are operating, and their lighting and heating are switched by an expert-rule fuzzy-logic controller acting on sensor set points, with no virtual model in the loop. The energy models were used for design and for offline analysis of logged data under hypothetical set points, so the study is a digital_model.

R1692.model_description: Physics-informed U-Net surrogate of Radiance ground-irradiance raytracing for tracked agrivoltaics
R1692.automated_input_evidence: we use historical data from the years 2010 to 2019, which were downloaded from the DWD21 open database.
R1692.actuation_evidence: Our surrogate model allows on-the-fly raytracing calculations for edge computing-based PV tracker applications
R1692.justification: A deep-learning surrogate of raytraced ground irradiance was trained and tested on public historical weather data and simulated maps of the Morschenich-Alt geometry. Use in tracker control at the edge is only mentioned as a future possibility, with no live data link and no actuation.

R1829.model_description: none; multilinear regression used only for PAR sensor calibration
R1829.automated_input_evidence: the raw data are stored in the SD card in a .txt file and later for calibration they will be analyzed using excel
R1829.justification: This is a low-cost PAR sensor whose multilinear regression converts spectral channel readings into PPFD. That is a measurement calibration, not a model of how the system behaves. The outputs are logged and shown on a dashboard, with no system model and no actuation.

R1969.automated_input_evidence: The LCD will display data from the three sensors.
R1969.actuation_evidence: If the value obtained from the three sensors does not reach the desired value, the controlling system consisting of a pump containing water will water the farm
R1969.justification: An Arduino prototype monitors soil moisture, temperature and pH, shows them on an LCD, and runs an irrigation pump when soil moisture crosses a threshold. There is no virtual model, so the study is pure sensing plus threshold control.

R2039.model_description: UAV photogrammetric 3D orchard model with pvlib PV-output and crop-irradiance simulation
R2039.automated_input_evidence: Simultaneously, real-time sensor data from the hardware is fed back into the digital twin to synchronise the virtual and physical states.
R2039.actuation_evidence: allowing the user to manually adjust the setpoints of the physical trackers via the dashboard interface.
R2039.justification: Sensor data stream through MQTT, Node-RED and InfluxDB into the 3D/pvlib environment, and this was shown on a physical tracker prototype. The tracker is actuated by a user who sets set-points on the dashboard, not by model outputs, so despite the authors' closed-loop claim the study is coded digital_shadow. The full text could show that live data only reach dashboards and not the pvlib model, which would lower it to digital_model.

R1141.model_description: PVGIS irradiance estimates with PV sizing and pump hydraulic (Bernoulli/Darcy-Weisbach) equations
R1141.automated_input_evidence: Based on the solar atlas of the year 2019, the horizontal global irradiance data of the sector were obtained. The PVGIS software was used to estimate the solar irradiance
R1141.actuation_evidence: It was configured an automatic irrigation two times per day, (6 am and 6 pm) with a duration of 5 minutes each.
R1141.justification: The physics-based models are static design sizing calculations driven by atlas/PVGIS irradiance, and no installation data feed them. Irrigation on the built 20 m2 prototype runs on a fixed timer schedule, which is rule-based and not model-driven.

R1199.automated_input_evidence: Data from these instruments were aggregated and logged through a remote terminal unit (RTU)
R1199.actuation_evidence: It adopts a straightforward yet effective approach to linearly adjust the panel’s tilt angle within preset maximum and minimum values, corresponding with the time of day
R1199.justification: The motorised foldable panels follow a time-based tracking rule, and the shadow-control set-points were found empirically. Sun-position and shadow-length geometry is the only modelling, which does not count as a virtual model. The testbed only logs data for comparison.

R1285.model_description: Bifacial Radiance ray-tracing irradiance model and PVWatts DC yield model
R1285.automated_input_evidence: Finally, EPW weather files were imported to simulate two representative days from the measurement period.
R1285.actuation_evidence: The tracking setup is controlled by a PLC that determines the position of the PV modules based on the position of the sun, irradiance level, windspeed, etc.
R1285.justification: The ray-tracing simulations use EPW weather files. Measured data go to a cloud database and are converted to yield afterwards with PVWatts, and no automated model ingestion is described. Tracker motion comes from a conventional PLC rule, with no model in the loop.

R1307.automated_input_evidence: The sensors were connected in parallel to give one integrated signal per PARbar that was recorded by a data logger.
R1307.justification: This is a pure light-sensing study (PARbars logged by data loggers) on a commercial raspberry agrivoltaic farm. The biomass = intercepted PAR x LUE equation is only a post-hoc diagnostic ratio, not a model of how the system behaves.

R1311.model_description: mechanistic soil-plant-atmosphere energy-balance canopy temperature model with simple raytracing
R1311.automated_input_evidence: Using only available entries readily measured in AVD systems, it simulates the temperature range of a canopy both in plain field and AVD systems.
R1311.actuation_evidence: More efforts are still required to make the model more robust before trusting it with steering PV panels in commercial settings.
R1311.justification: The model is meant to steer the panels, but the text never says how the AVD sensor data reach it, and its outputs are also described as passed to the grower. Following the protocol, the lower level is coded. The only results are a comparison with hand-held IR thermometer readings and simulations on historical 2019 data.

R1359.automated_input_evidence: Original SM records and climatic data have been imported and will be stored and managed in a time series database (InfluxDB) and a connected visualization tool (Grafana).
R1359.justification: This is soil-moisture monitoring with a database and Grafana dashboards. ET is derived straight from measured soil moisture declines by a water balance, and the FAO-56 ETP serves only as a reference check for the open field. Nothing models the installation's behaviour and nothing actuates.

R3239.model_description: AVrain physics-based geometric rain redistribution model, coupled offline to Hydrus-2D soil water model
R3239.automated_input_evidence: The rain redistribution model AVrain was tested for 11 rain events
R3239.actuation_evidence: minimizing rain interception by the panels by deciding their titling angle based on wind direction
R3239.justification: AVrain is a validated physics-based model, but it was run offline in R on recorded event data, and the panel avoidance strategy was a wind-direction rule with no model in the loop. The claim that it 'allows real-time strategies' is a potential use that the paper neither designs as an architecture nor runs.

R0323.model_description: Ecotect simulation of PAR and sunshine-hour distribution under oblique single-axis trackers
R0323.automated_input_evidence: Use Autodesk Ecotect Analysis to build the oblique single-axis tracking agrivoltaic system described above.
R0323.actuation_evidence: When the solar radiation exceeds LSP or is less than 50% of LSP, the system can maximizes the shading area.
R0323.justification: The light model is a pure simulation of a hypothetical site. The proposed tracking algorithm is a rule based on sun-position geometry and light-saturation thresholds, applied only in simulation for one day, with no model in the loop and no hardware.

R0352.model_description: Exergy-based greenhouse heat deviation model with real-time energy scheduling optimization
R0352.automated_input_evidence: Input day-ahead and real-time solar irradiance, outdoor temperature, electric loads, thermal loads and other data, and input various parameters required in the calculation model
R0352.actuation_evidence: so that develop the real-time adjustment plan of energy storage and electric loads
R0352.justification: A physics-based thermal and exergy model plus an optimization scheduler is evaluated as a calculation case study using greenhouse data. The text describes no software data link from the installation and no automatic execution of the plans on storage or loads.

R0415.automated_input_evidence: The measured data by each sensor and inverter were stored in a web server by TCP/IP communication
R0415.actuation_evidence: Smart farming system, in turn, is enabled by the growth environment data from the web server, which provides an automated schedule to control the amount of water supply
R0415.justification: The vineyard test bed streams sensor and inverter data to a web server for a monitoring page, and it schedules irrigation automatically from those data. No model of system behavior is described, so this is sensing, monitoring and rule-based control.

R0590.model_description: none (parametric OpenSCAD geometry script and material-cost calculation only)
R0590.actuation_evidence: future work could integrate a temperature sensor, fan and/or a motor to control air inflow into the greenhouse box to regulate its temperature using an Arduino microcontroller
R0590.justification: The POSCAS invention is a parametric CAD design with a cost analysis. It has no model of light, energy, crop or microclimate behavior, and the sensor-based automation appears only as future work.

R0700.model_description: 2D view-factor radiation model with Perez transposition, PVWatts energy model and LCOE KPIs
R0700.automated_input_evidence: the diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) and direct normal irradiance (DNI) inputs are taken from the TMY pvgis database
R0700.justification: The webtool runs pre-computed simulations from typical-year weather data and user-set geometry. It has no link to any specific installation and gives outputs only to people as design guidance.

R2177.model_description: radiation model for mono/bifacial panels with rule- and optimization-based tilt control
R2177.automated_input_evidence: We compare different variants of the proposed schemes across multiple crop light requirements and DC/AC ratios through 384 simulations.
R2177.actuation_evidence: a proactive, model-based control algorithm that determines panel tilt angles based on weather forecasts while respecting constraints such as inverter capacity
R2177.justification: A radiation model drives tilt control, but its inputs are weather forecasts, and the closed loop exists only in 384 simulations; the abstract does not say whether installation data feed the reactive light-target adjustment. Automated input is unclear, so the lower level is assigned.

R2220.model_description: U-Net++ segmentation, EfficientNet-B3 stress classifier, CNN LAI regressor (image-based)
R2220.automated_input_evidence: This method implemented the control of cucumber plant shading and irrigation in real time using monitored plant vigor.
R2220.actuation_evidence: Shading and irrigation control relied on monitored plant vigor assessed using a U-Net++ implementation for canopy segmentation, an EfficientNet-B3 implementation for stress differentiation
R2220.justification: Shading and irrigation control is driven by CNN image segmentation and classification of plant vigor, which are perception models and not models of system behavior. The yield results are described as simulated and no crop or microclimate model is named, so the lower level (NA) is assigned.

R2234.model_description: solar-trajectory shadow analysis and minute-level dynamic PV power generation model
R2234.automated_input_evidence: a minute-level precision dynamic photovoltaic power generation model that integrates real-time meteorological data to achieve continuous output power evaluation and system performance monitoring
R2234.actuation_evidence: providing quantitative decision support for agrivoltaic system design
R2234.justification: The shadow and PV power models support design optimization of tilt and spacing. The abstract mentions real-time meteorological data but does not say they come automatically from a specific installation, so digital_model is assigned.

R2254.model_description: mathematical light/power model with mixed-integer tilt optimization
R2254.automated_input_evidence: the results of numerical simulations are reported and discussed, using real-world data based on an existing agrivoltaic plant in Southern Italy.
R2254.actuation_evidence: a novel optimization-based approach for automatically controlling the balance between the crops’ light exposure and the power generation
R2254.justification: An optimization model is designed to set tilt automatically, but it is evaluated only in numerical simulations using plant data, with no automated link to the installation. With no automated input, the level is digital_model.

R2264.model_description: multiple linear regression and tree-based ensemble crop yield response models
R2264.automated_input_evidence: This study evaluates yield responses across a global dataset of 546 observations from 66 studies
R2264.justification: Data-driven crop yield response models are fitted to a pooled literature dataset, with no link to any specific installation. This is a digital_model at most.

R2286.automated_input_evidence: A comprehensive network of over 80 sensors is being deployed across the site to monitor environmental, agricultural, and PV variables in real-time.
R2286.justification: The study describes sensor instrumentation and monitoring of a pilot agrivoltaic site, and no virtual model is mentioned. Pure sensing is NA.

R2288.automated_input_evidence: provides the foundation for future integration with predictive models and energy-use optimization strategies
R2288.actuation_evidence: The architecture includes a network of calibrated sensors, programmable logic for irrigation control, and centralized data logging for analysis.
R2288.justification: The system has monitoring plus irrigation driven by sensor feedback through programmable logic, and predictive models are left explicitly to future work. Rule-based control without a model is NA.

R2293.automated_input_evidence: data collection and transmission are carried out via ZigBee wireless communication to achieve system data monitoring and real-time control
R2293.actuation_evidence: integrates microcontroller technology, wireless network technology, monitoring configuration technology, and solar photovoltaic power generation technology to design an intelligent control system for photovoltaic greenhouses
R2293.justification: This is a microcontroller and ZigBee monitoring and control system with no virtual model. The control appears to be direct sensor-based control, so it is NA.

R2299.actuation_evidence: The generated solar power was utilized to operate LED lights for supplemental illumination during low-light conditions
R2299.justification: A field trellis agrivoltaic setup with LED lighting switched on in low light; 'agrovoltaic model' refers to the farming concept, not a computational model. No virtual model, so NA.

R2332.actuation_evidence: A low-cost photovoltaic (PV)-powered microclimate control system was deployed to regulate temperature, humidity, and vapor pressure deficit while sustaining electricity generation.
R2332.justification: A low-cost microclimate controller regulates temperature, RH and VPD in experimental PV greenhouses, and no virtual model is described. It is coded as sensor-based control, NA.

R2877.automated_input_evidence: Microclimate was monitored with an IoT sensor network (air and soil temperature, humidity, PAR)
R2877.actuation_evidence: Key engineering aspects include strong support structures, effective shading, and integrated monitoring for data-driven control.
R2877.justification: This is a hortivoltaic pilot with IoT microclimate monitoring and descriptive results, and no virtual model is mentioned. Raw-data monitoring is NA.

R2806.model_description: unspecified optimization algorithm for moving flexible PV modules
R2806.automated_input_evidence: During the project, the PV performance in terms of efficiency and electricity production will be continuously monitored.
R2806.actuation_evidence: The movement of the PV modules will be automated and controlled through customizable control and management logic, aiming at obtaining an optimal trade-off condition between crop and energy yields.
R2806.justification: The planned automated PV-module movement uses an unspecified algorithm or logic, and it is not stated whether a crop or energy model sits in the loop. Because the virtual model is unclear, the lower level (NA) is assigned; nothing has been built yet.

R2485.model_description: yield projection model under varying shade factors
R2485.justification: This four-year field trial of fixed agrivoltaics includes model projections of 10-year yield under different shade factors. The model is offline with no automated data link, so it is a digital_model.

R2549.model_description: three-layer PV-battery capacity, scheduling and real-time control optimization model
R2549.automated_input_evidence: a supply–demand matching coefficient was developed and applied to a year-long tomato cultivation experiment, quantifying significant mismatches.
R2549.actuation_evidence: systematically coordinating capacity design, weekly scheduling, and real-time control with growth stages to eliminate the adaptation inefficiencies inherent in the conventional approach
R2549.justification: An optimization framework, including a real-time control layer, is evaluated through comparative economic results that appear to be simulated. The abstract does not state that installation data are ingested automatically or that actuation runs on hardware, so the lower level is assigned.

R2562.model_description: solar geometry plus ray-tracing real-time greenhouse shadow prediction model
R2562.automated_input_evidence: served as the basis for a real-time model predicting greenhouse shadows by integrating solar geometry and ray-tracing algorithms
R2562.actuation_evidence: this study developed a dynamic tracking photovoltaic greenhouse (TPVG) system
R2562.justification: A ray-tracing shadow model is built for a physical tracking PV greenhouse, but the abstract does not say whether installation data feed it or whether it drives the tracker. Both links are unclear, so digital_model is assigned.

R2591.automated_input_evidence: Extensive experiments on real agricultural vision benchmarks and agrivoltaic shadow variants demonstrate that PrivAgriVolt improves stress recognition and segmentation under PV shading
R2591.justification: This is a federated image-recognition framework for crop stress, which is an image classifier that does not model system behavior, and it is evaluated on public benchmarks. It is coded NA.

R2624.model_description: empirical enthalpy-photosynthetic rate relationship for strawberries
R2624.actuation_evidence: a dynamic regulation strategy was proposed using the critical enthalpy value as a threshold
R2624.justification: The proposed regulation is threshold-based on a critical enthalpy value, derived from an empirical analysis of photosynthesis. Whether a behavioral or energy model is used is unclear, so the lower level (NA) is assigned.

R2662.model_description: PV-induced microclimate, soil-water dynamics and energy production simulation models
R2662.automated_input_evidence: This paper proposes a simulation-driven cyber-physical architecture for Smart Agrivoltaics, designed as an evolution of an existing IoT-based irrigation and hydraulic anomaly-detection platform
R2662.actuation_evidence: The proposed simulation framework integrates an actively controlled photovoltaic layer with distributed environmental sensing, energy-aware irrigation scheduling, and real-time flow-based leak detection.
R2662.justification: The proposed cyber-physical architecture couples IoT sensing with simulation models and active control of shading and irrigation, which is a designed twin. It is evaluated only by comparative simulation, so nothing was demonstrated on hardware.

R2695.model_description: PVsyst PV energy yield and economic simulation
R2695.automated_input_evidence: The system's performance and economic viability were assessed with PVsyst software.
R2695.actuation_evidence: Only the Building Integrated Photovoltaic greenhouse was able to consistently maintain a suitable environment (temperature ≤25 °C, humidity ≥65%) after system activation.
R2695.justification: Sensor monitoring and an environmental control system run in experimental greenhouses, while PVsyst is used offline for energy and economic assessment. The model has no automated input, so the level is digital_model.

R0804.model_description: conceptual growth and irrigation models calculating section irrigation rates (unspecified)
R0804.automated_input_evidence: The obtained data are sent to the control center, where they are entered into mathematical models of growth, irrigation, etc.
R0804.actuation_evidence: the control system determines the sections and irrigation rates. Railer receives the necessary data from the control system (section, volume) and transmits the results in real time.
R0804.justification: The concept sends section sensor data to growth/irrigation models in a control center, and the control system automatically sends irrigation rates to an automated railer, so the design is a twin. The models are only named, not specified, and nothing was built; panel rotation follows fixed rules.

R0838.model_description: CNN leaf-disease image classifier only; no system-behavior model
R0838.automated_input_evidence: The sensor data along with image data will be sent to the cloud for visualisation and further processing of image data to predict the growth rate of the crop.
R0838.actuation_evidence: Fan will be turned on for ventilation or cooling when the sensed temperature value is greater than the threshold value
R0838.justification: The small Raspberry Pi greenhouse prototype uses a CNN disease classifier, threshold-based actuator control and a Blynk dashboard; the growth-rate prediction is mentioned once and never described. No virtual model of system behavior exists, so the level is NA.

R0909.model_description: AI steering algorithm combining sensors with mechanistic crop models (designed); Penman-Monteith ETo analysis
R0909.automated_input_evidence: Variables that are difficult to evaluate continuously in the field such as predawn water potential can be estimated by crop models and used to take decisions
R0909.actuation_evidence: we propose to use an artificial intelligence to pilot the orientation of solar panels using environmental and plant indicators derived from both sensors and crop models.
R0909.justification: The proposed sensor-plus-crop-model AI steering is only a conceptual algorithm; the paper says it is under evaluation at Tresserre but reports no results from it. The results come from a fixed afternoon-shading policy at Piolenc, with ETo computed offline using Penman-Monteith from site data, so only the digital model level is demonstrated.

R1076.model_description: photosynthesis-rate light-response model and annual energy/water balance calculations
R1076.automated_input_evidence: continuous recording of data (for example in the cloud), which are subsequently subject to automatic analysis
R1076.actuation_evidence: Based on the estimated parameter values, a method of controlling the climatic conditions in the tunnel was proposed.
R1076.justification: A photosynthesis model and energy/water balance analyses are used to set solar-underexposure thresholds and a proposed control method. The packet is cut off before the control-algorithm chapters, so whether the model runs in a live loop is unclear, and the lower level is chosen.

R1084.model_description: Ladybug/Radiance ray-tracing ground irradiance model of the PV array
R1084.automated_input_evidence: The model used the Fort Collins-Loveland Municipal Airport TMY3 file.
R1084.justification: An irradiance model of the testbed array is driven by a TMY3 weather file, and the microclimate is logged separately on HOBO USB loggers. No automated link to the model and no actuation are described, so the level is digital model.

R1134.model_description: planned AI/ML crop-yield prediction model (digital twin), not yet developed
R1134.automated_input_evidence: A framework is proposed to exploit Internet of Things (IoT) concepts, with a sensor network to collect data on the field merged with sensor fusion
R1134.justification: Despite the digital twin title, the lysimeter testbed only logs sensor data to a data logger, and the yield prediction model is left to future work. Sensor data are described as input for building the model rather than as a live feed into it, so the design is coded digital model and the demonstrated system is pure sensing (NA).

R0200.model_description: none stated; OPV greenhouse analysis method not described
R0200.justification: The one-sentence abstract says OPV greenhouses are 'analysed' but does not say whether a light, crop or energy model is used. Treated as unclear and coded at the lower level; the full text could show a digital model.

R0268.actuation_evidence: by comparing fixed and dynamic systems with two different orientation policies
R0268.justification: This is an experimental field comparison of fixed and tracking PV over lettuce, and the trackers follow fixed orientation policies. The abstract describes no virtual model.

R3144.actuation_evidence: flexible solar panels/thin films which are programmed to deploy automatically, based on measured sunlight at any given time
R3144.justification: The folding PV screen deploys directly from measured sunlight, which is sensor-based rule control with no virtual model. The abstract does not report a built or tested prototype.

R0367.model_description: PV array power prediction simulation used to tune fuzzy MPPT parameters
R0367.automated_input_evidence: Calculations and simulation of power prediction algorithm were carried out for obtaining the suitable parameters and duty cycle of the fuzzy control algorithm
R0367.actuation_evidence: the fuzzy control algorithm, to modulate output power in real-time
R0367.justification: A PV power simulation is used offline to tune a fuzzy MPPT controller. The real-time converter control is rule-based and has no model with live input in the loop.

R0462.model_description: MATLAB/Simulink PV array and MPPT simulation model
R0462.automated_input_evidence: Through the MPPT modelling and simulation in MATLAB/Simulink and the corresponding circuit test
R0462.actuation_evidence: this paper proposes a new variable-step conductance increment method to track the maximum power point
R0462.justification: An offline Simulink PV/MPPT model is used to evaluate a rule-based incremental-conductance MPPT algorithm, and a circuit test was run. No installation data feed the model.

R0490.model_description: reduced-order ray-tracing solar power flow model with genomic ML optimization
R0490.automated_input_evidence: Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the results
R0490.justification: Although the authors call it a 'Digital-Twin', this is a computational design framework run on numerical examples. It has no link to a physical installation.

R0497.actuation_evidence: as per scheduled operations of airflow, photosynthetically active radiation for improved photosynthesis, climate control, and backup battery energy source
R0497.justification: This is a hardware prototype power optimizer with MPPT and scheduled load operation. 'Virtual asymmetry' is an electrical mismatch effect, not a virtual model.

R0524.actuation_evidence: the use of intelligent equipment to achieve real-time tracking of the sun's rays
R0524.justification: The abstract describes sun tracking and greenhouse parameter regulation in general terms. It names no virtual model and no implemented system.

R0531.actuation_evidence: coordinated, unified control and monitoring architecture is developed to manage the PV-GH internal parameters within defined boundary conditions
R0531.justification: An ATmega 2560 controller keeps greenhouse parameters within defined boundaries, which is threshold control with no virtual model. Hardware appears to have been developed, but the paper is mainly conceptual.

R0534.model_description: CFD fluid dynamics and temperature simulation of greenhouse microclimate
R0534.automated_input_evidence: the results of microclimates greenhouse monitoring can be seen by users through smartphones
R0534.actuation_evidence: combination of the use of ventilation, horizontal air flow (HAF) fan, and exhaust fan can be utilized to maintain temperature and humidity
R0534.justification: A design-stage CFD microclimate simulation is the only virtual model. IoT monitoring goes to a smartphone display, and the fan and ventilation control appears range-based.

R0621.model_description: semivariogram/kriging geostatistical model of PPFD and DLI distribution
R0621.automated_input_evidence: Following semivariogram and kriging approach, spatial variation of PPFD and DLI was quantified within the AVS.
R0621.justification: Kriging maps of light built from measurements at the 105 kWp AVS form an offline data-driven light model. The abstract shows no automated data link and no actuation.

R0648.model_description: data-driven crop yield and monetary performance estimation model in DSS
R0648.automated_input_evidence: the real-time monitoring data is used as an input of the DSS system for performance estimation of an APV system in terms of production yields of crops and monetary benefit
R0648.actuation_evidence: The proposed DSS is devised to provide a mobile application service, satellite image processing, real-time data monitoring, and performance estimation.
R0648.justification: Real-time sensor data from an actual APV feed a performance-estimation model whose outputs go to farmers through a DSS. The full text could show that the field validation was run offline.

R0652.model_description: geometric ray-tracing light/power model with genomic-based optimization
R0652.justification: A purely computational ray-tracing design framework, despite the 'digital-twin' label. It has no physical installation link.

R0803.model_description: solar explorer web tool theoretical PV annual production estimate
R0803.automated_input_evidence: compare the actual annual production of each greenhouse with the theoretical annual production estimated with the solar explorer web tool
R0803.justification: Measured production from the vendor web platforms is compared offline with a theoretical PV estimate. The model receives no installation data automatically.

R0867.automated_input_evidence: To measure the temperature, humidity, moisture, and the PV panel output voltage, current a microcontroller-based data logger is designed.
R0867.justification: This is pure data acquisition with a microcontroller data logger on an experimental prototype. There is no virtual model.

R0889.model_description: PV energy harvesting and irrigation demand simulation
R0889.automated_input_evidence: The required amount of water for irrigation and the number of solar photovoltaic (PV) panels are calculated considering the rainfall and shadow impact, respectively.
R0889.actuation_evidence: The designed system can automatically turn on the irrigation based on the sensor data and can be controlled and monitored remotely.
R0889.justification: An offline sizing simulation gives a digital model, and the irrigation switches on directly from sensor data with no model in the loop. Neither element makes it a shadow or twin.

R0901.automated_input_evidence: the solar output electrical parameters voltage and current are measured hourly using data logger of Arduino
R0901.actuation_evidence: Development of a Vertical Agri-voltaic with Self-Powered Automated Irrigation System
R0901.justification: This is a barrel-scale prototype with an Arduino data logger and automated irrigation. No virtual model is described.

R0921.automated_input_evidence: soil characteristics such as moisture, NPK content, electrical conductivity and pH were monitored using IoT technology for real-time tracking during the 40-day development period
R0921.justification: This is a pilot crop-shading experiment with IoT soil monitoring only. There is no virtual model and no actuation.

R3082.automated_input_evidence: the carrier kinetics and kinematics are modeled and validated through simulations
R3082.actuation_evidence: position and trajectory controllers are designed and simulations are presented
R3082.justification: The only model is of the cleaning robot's dynamics, not of a light, PV energy, crop, microclimate or water subsystem, and its control is only simulated. It is an initial design with no hardware run.

R0970.automated_input_evidence: This paper presents a flexible, customizable, reliable sensor node and open platform.
R0970.justification: This is an open-platform sensor node for data acquisition. No virtual model or model-driven control is described.

R1035.automated_input_evidence: two testbeds were designed and a series of experiments in PA was performed
R1035.justification: This is a wireless communication interference study on testbeds for solar insecticidal lamps. There is no virtual model of system behavior.

R1105.model_description: PV power generation and shading simulation for single-axis tracking strategies
R1105.actuation_evidence: During the production season, the dynamic PV systems switch to the shadow-free mode to ensure the photosynthesis of crops within the CSGs.
R1105.justification: Simulations of the tracking strategies form an offline digital model. The trackers follow predefined strategies and seasonal mode switches, with no automated installation data feeding a model.

R1108.model_description: none stated; technical-economic analysis method not described
R1108.justification: A short techno-economic feasibility abstract that does not say whether a PV yield model was used. Coded at the lower level; the full text could show a digital model.

R1149.model_description: none implemented; AI/big-data predictive model planned
R1149.automated_input_evidence: develop an infrastructure suitable for implementing a predictive model based on artificial intelligence and big data
R1149.actuation_evidence: SolarFertigation can monitor and optimize fertigation autonomously, based on the analysis of data collected through the cloud.
R1149.justification: Cloud-based autonomous fertigation was field-tested, but the AI predictive model is only planned, and the current 'analysis of data' may be rule-based. The full text could show a model in the loop.

R1202.model_description: simplified agrivoltaic model for greenhouse cover transparency factor
R1202.automated_input_evidence: estimate the appropriate transparency level of a solar greenhouse covers according to the characteristics of the crop and the location, using a simplified agrivoltaic model
R1202.justification: A design-support interface runs a simplified agrivoltaic model on crop and location inputs. 'Real-time' refers to computation speed, not live installation data.

R1204.model_description: none stated; techno-economic metrics computed, model unclear
R1204.automated_input_evidence: transmitting the data wirelessly to a centralized database for processing and analysis
R1204.actuation_evidence: Farmers can remotely access vital information through a user-friendly web interface, monitor crop parameters, track changes, and receive alerts about irrigation needs.
R1204.justification: Sensor data go to a database and web dashboard with irrigation alerts, and the 'automated' irrigation appears sensor-driven. Whether any PV or crop model underlies the techno-economic assessment is unclear.

R1211.model_description: lighting simulation model; AI-based greenhouse control of unclear nature
R1211.automated_input_evidence: A sensor network monitors indoor environmental variables, and a weather station monitors outdoor environmental variables.
R1211.actuation_evidence: A computational system based on artificial intelligence is responsible for the autonomous control of the greenhouses.
R1211.justification: The lighting system was designed with an offline simulation model, which supports digital_model. The AI autonomous control may or may not contain a model fed by sensor data, so the full text could raise the level.

R1231.automated_input_evidence: focuses on energy-efficient data aggregation and classification for monitoring agrovoltaics using real-time data
R1231.justification: The ML component only classifies monitoring data into crop-health and panel-condition states and does not model system behavior. There is no actuation.

R2994.automated_input_evidence: with an IoT-based monitoring system as an alternative agro-shade material
R2994.actuation_evidence: generate power for the IoT monitoring system and control environmental variables like temperature, humidity, and light intensity
R2994.justification: This is a small FSC-roofed greenhouse prototype with IoT monitoring and environmental control. No virtual model is described.

R1279.actuation_evidence: Experiments had been conducted to enhance light-dependent resistor (LDR) accuracy for tracking, exploring shielding and tradeoffs.
R1279.justification: This is a solar tree prototype with LDR-based sun tracking, which is direct sensor control with no virtual model.

R1367.model_description: GWO-BP neural network greenhouse temperature forecaster; PV array layout architectural model
R1367.automated_input_evidence: Our MATLAB simulation analysis reveals that the GWO-BP prediction method exhibits higher accuracy compared to traditional prediction methods.
R1367.actuation_evidence: we introduce an improved APSO-optimized fuzzy PID algorithm (APSO-FUZZY-PID) and compare its control effects with two other temperature control models
R1367.justification: A GWO-BP temperature forecaster exists, but it is evaluated only in MATLAB simulation, and the abstract does not say the LoRa/NB-IoT monitoring data feed it. The fuzzy-PID temperature control is feedback/rule control with no virtual model in the loop.

R1384.model_description: irradiance correlation for indoor light; unclear if a system model
R1384.automated_input_evidence: The Internet of Things (IoT) technology was integrated into the system to remotely monitor the variations in ambient light, solar irradiance, and energy consumption of the artificial lighting system.
R1384.actuation_evidence: An adaptive control algorithm based on the correlation of outdoor solar irradiance and the ambient light inside the solar greenhouse was developed to dynamically adjust the illuminance of artificial lights.
R1384.justification: The dimming algorithm maps measured irradiance to lamp output through a correlation, which may be a rule-like control law rather than a model of the system's behaviour. Because the virtual model cannot be judged, the lower level applies.

R1397.model_description: none; CNN crop-counting image classifiers only
R1397.actuation_evidence: The experimental setup includes a solar-powered greenhouse with IoT-controlled micro-climate management to ensure optimal growing conditions.
R1397.justification: The only models are CNN image classifiers that count chili fruit, and these do not model system behaviour. The IoT microclimate control has no virtual model in the loop.

R1443.model_description: ML analytics with multi-objective optimization of louvre angle (architecture only)
R1443.automated_input_evidence: The proposed DSS integrates and synchronizes multi-sensor data acquisition, data quality management, machine learning and analytics
R1443.actuation_evidence: multi-objective optimization for adaptive control of the louvre to a specified angle position
R1443.justification: The blueprint feeds sensor data into ML and optimization models that set the louvre angle in real time, which is a designed twin. Implementation is ongoing and nothing was run on hardware.

R1452.model_description: none; sun-altitude and growth-stage tilt rules
R1452.actuation_evidence: A linear motor–based folding tracking mechanism is introduced to automatically adjust the tilt angle of the PV modules according to the sun’s altitude and the crop growth stage
R1452.justification: Tilt is set from sun altitude and crop growth stage, which is sun-position and rule-based actuation with no virtual model. An 8 kW prototype was tested.

R1531.automated_input_evidence: Real-time data collection was performed using an IoT platform integrated with an ESP32 microcontroller and visualized through the Blynk dashboard.
R1531.justification: This is a fixed-tilt APV prototype with IoT sensing and a dashboard of raw values. No virtual model or actuation is described.

R1540.model_description: PAR and evapotranspiration shading analysis; model type not stated
R1540.actuation_evidence: integrating conventional solar tracking with dual-use water systems for irrigation and module cleaning
R1540.justification: The system uses conventional solar tracking and combined cleaning-irrigation, with 6 months of operation reported. The shading analysis of PAR and evapotranspiration may or may not use a virtual model, so the lower level is chosen.

R1541.model_description: none; MILP IoT gateway-placement optimizer, not a system-behavior model
R1541.automated_input_evidence: We evaluate the model on a 10 hectare agrivoltaic pilot facility at the University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil
R1541.justification: The MILP optimizes network gateway placement and does not model the light, PV, crop, microclimate or water behaviour of the installation. This is a planning analysis with no data link or actuation.

R1618.model_description: climate-adaptive crop model with irrigation and nutrient optimization (vaguely described)
R1618.automated_input_evidence: Soil moisture, crop status, and environmental data are continuously monitored to assist climate-adaptive crop modeling, optimal irrigation scheduling, enhanced crop health assessment, and enhanced energy management.
R1618.actuation_evidence: the nutrient optimization module, which dynamically regulates fertilizer supply based on information from soil nutrient sensor readings and crop growth phases
R1618.justification: Continuous monitoring is designed to feed adaptive crop modelling, but fertilizer regulation appears to be driven by sensor readings rather than by the model, so actuation is unclear. Validation is described as MATLAB simulation plus vague 'real-world case studies', with no clear hardware run of the model data flows.

R1626.automated_input_evidence: Real-time monitoring and control of environmental and operational variables are achieved through a wireless interface using NI myRIO-1900 and LabVIEW, enabling remote supervision.
R1626.actuation_evidence: The proposed agrivoltaic system features a solar tracking mechanism controlled by a proportional-integral (PI) controller
R1626.justification: Tracking uses a PI feedback controller and the system offers remote monitoring and supervision. No virtual model is described.

R1629.model_description: none; LDR-based tracking and soil-moisture irrigation control
R1629.automated_input_evidence: An Arduino-based monitoring system is also implemented to monitor the status of the agrivoltaic system, collect and analyze environmental parameters
R1629.actuation_evidence: The system features a single-axis solar tracking mechanism, incorporating Light Dependent Resistor (LDR) sensors
R1629.justification: Tracking is driven by LDR sensors and irrigation is driven by soil moisture, both sensor-based control. Monitoring has no virtual model.

R1636.automated_input_evidence: The proposed facility is designed to enable controlled experimentation, real-time monitoring, and optimization of key parameters such as energy efficiency, crop yield, microclimatic conditions
R1636.actuation_evidence: The laboratory integrates modern photovoltaic technologies, sensor networks, IoT platforms, and automated irrigation systems
R1636.justification: This is a conceptual laboratory with sensors, IoT and automated irrigation, and no virtual model is named. The abstract is too thin to rule out a shading model in the full paper.

R1637.model_description: greenhouse irradiance distribution model validated against measurements
R1637.automated_input_evidence: In parallel, an irradiance model tailored to this specific setup was developed using an existing model architecture.
R1637.actuation_evidence: dynamic photovoltaic panels were integrated in a Nordic greenhouse and controlled based on incoming irradiance
R1637.justification: The panel controller acts on measured incoming irradiance. The irradiance model was developed 'in parallel' and validated offline against the campaign data, so it is a digital model with no automated link and no control role. The full text could show the controller using the model.

R1638.model_description: none; SNN data classifier for sensor-data aggregation
R1638.justification: The work is a WSN data-aggregation scheme that uses a Conv1D/SNN classifier and a redundancy threshold, and it does not model agrivoltaic system behaviour. No installation actuation is involved.

R1711.model_description: none described; monitoring and analytics platform
R1711.automated_input_evidence: offer operators in this new sector a platform as a tool to have a global view of the system and optimise the agricultural and energy production
R1711.justification: This is a monitoring and analytics platform for operators. The abstract names no model of system behaviour, so whether its 'advanced analytics' include a virtual model cannot be judged.

R1722.model_description: block-cooling and PV-battery energy model of photovoltaic greenhouse
R1722.actuation_evidence: decoupled temperature and humidity control is proposed and realised via the proportion-integration-differentiation (PID) controller
R1722.justification: A physics-based cooling-load and energy model is analysed with PID/PI controllers, apparently in simulation. No automated installation data or model-driven actuation is reported.

R1762.model_description: AI-based predictive analysis of greenhouse conditions (unspecified)
R1762.automated_input_evidence: The physical domain integrates sensors and actuators, while the cyber domain processes data via artificial intelligence and cloud services.
R1762.actuation_evidence: to facilitate real-time monitoring, predictive analysis, and dynamic control of greenhouse conditions
R1762.justification: Cloud AI processes sensor data from the Savona prototype for predictive analysis. However, whether 'dynamic control' is driven automatically by the model or goes through the GUI user cannot be judged, so the lower level is chosen.

R1800.automated_input_evidence: This MNA sensor should be capable of continuous data acquisition in real-time using electronic sensing of versatile physiological aspects
R1800.justification: This is a planned microneedle impedance sensor for plant monitoring, with data categorization only. No virtual model or actuation is described.

R1811.automated_input_evidence: A low cost dedicated monitoring system is going to be implemented in order to store data related to indoor and outdoor sensor measurements.
R1811.actuation_evidence: The proposal introduces a tracking system based on a logic designed to maximize the agro-energy yield of the agrivoltaic system.
R1811.justification: This is a project proposal with rule-based tracking 'logic' and a monitoring system that only stores data. The full text could reveal a model behind the tracking logic.

R1814.model_description: first-principles PV greenhouse model for energy, water, yield, quality
R1814.automated_input_evidence: embeds real-time cost–revenue analysis into control logic
R1814.actuation_evidence: Implemented as a low-cost digital twin, the framework supports adaptive, quality-aware greenhouse control
R1814.justification: A first-principles model was validated against a 97-day field crop cycle. The abstract does not show sensor data streaming into it or its outputs driving actuators, and the 'digital twin' label alone is not evidence, so the lower level is chosen.

R1823.model_description: dynamic crop model with shading factors, MATLAB simulation
R1823.automated_input_evidence: Real-time data analytics is employed to improve water conservation, crop health prediction, and energy efficiency.
R1823.justification: The framework is designed to feed LoRaWAN/PLC sensor data to real-time analytics and a dynamic crop model, but no automated actuation is described. The experimental demonstration 'is performed in MATLAB', with no clear hardware run of the data flows.

R2900.model_description: PCA and K-means exploratory analysis; yield model unclear
R2900.automated_input_evidence: Environmental parameters were monitored at 15 minute intervals, while strawberry production data were collected as daily aggregates.
R2900.justification: Monitoring data were analysed offline with PCA and clustering. Whether a working ML yield model of the system was built is unclear because label sparsity is said to hinder supervised learning.

R1871.model_description: simulation model of PV MPPT power electronics and irrigation load
R1871.automated_input_evidence: presents simulation-based tests of the modified MPPT and coupled non-linear digital irrigation control system
R1871.actuation_evidence: a prototype Integrated Energy Management and Control System (EMCS) for off-grid agrivoltaics implementations used in irrigation applications is presented
R1871.justification: The PV and irrigation power system is modelled and tested in simulation, which makes it a digital model. MPPT and irrigation control are feedback controllers, and a simulated loop is not a demonstration.

R1896.actuation_evidence: By selectively controlling panel deployment during midday peaks, solar power generation is maximized at times of reduced plant photosynthetic efficiency.
R1896.justification: Panels are deployed on a time-of-day rule (11 a.m. to 2 p.m.) in a plant-factory pilot. No virtual model is described.

R1932.model_description: automation models for fertigation scheduling; nature unclear
R1932.automated_input_evidence: It enables precise, adaptive management of fertigation processes based on real-time environmental, agronomic, and operational data
R1932.actuation_evidence: The new cloud-based architecture introduces advanced automation models that adjust fertigation schedules dynamically according to crop phenology, weather conditions, soil characteristics, topography, and machine status
R1932.justification: It cannot be judged whether the 'automation models' are crop or water models or scheduling rules, so the lower level applies. Field validation covered only LoRaWAN coverage and radiation measurements.

R2062.model_description: MPC with PV power, shading factor and crop yield models
R2062.automated_input_evidence: given solar irradiance and ambient temperature measurements
R2062.actuation_evidence: dynamically adjusts panel positions in real time to maximize power production and crop yield
R2062.justification: The MPC is designed to take real-time measurements and set dual-axis panel positions automatically, which is a designed twin. Only simulated case studies are reported, and a simulated closed loop does not count as a demonstration.

R2108.automated_input_evidence: IoT based sensors, which monitor soil moisture, weather data, and crop conditions in real time
R2108.actuation_evidence: A smart irrigation mechanism uses this data to automate water distribution
R2108.justification: Irrigation is automated directly from sensor data with no virtual model. No hardware results are reported.

R2171.actuation_evidence: This paper proposes a novel sustainable, energy-positive, fully automated, and AI-controlled Outdoor Agrivoltaic Vertical Farming (OAVF) system.
R2171.justification: The system is called 'AI-controlled', but the abstract names no model of system behaviour and no data flow. The lower level is chosen pending the full text.

R2824.actuation_evidence: By shortening OPV deployment duration from 24 to 6 h, the system preserves crop yields
R2824.justification: The foldable OPV shade is deployed on a time schedule in an operating greenhouse trial. No virtual model is described.

R2176.model_description: data-driven irrigation soil-water module; PV cleaning economic model
R2176.automated_input_evidence: integrates multi-parameter field monitoring, edge and cloud-based data management, environmental and crop monitoring, a data-driven irrigation module
R2176.actuation_evidence: the proposed system transforms real-time field observations into operational recommendations for irrigation, PV operation, and economic management
R2176.justification: The platform is designed to feed IoT data to models that output recommendations for people, which is a designed shadow. Irrigation was 'retrospectively assessed' and the cleaning/tilt modules were not validated, so it is unclear that a live automated model link was run, and the lower level is chosen.

R2517.model_description: Shading (ground irradiance) simulation and PV performance model validated against field measurements
R2517.automated_input_evidence: raw files from the dataloggers are uploaded every 24 h to a cloud-based server via a router.
R2517.actuation_evidence: This latter aspect is also optimized by the possibility of manually adjust the tilt of the panels when needed due to agricultural management requirements.
R2517.justification: Shading and PV simulation models are run offline and compared with monitoring data; the automatic datalogger upload goes to cloud storage, and nothing in the text says it feeds the models. Panel tilt is adjusted manually, so there is no model-driven actuation.

R2529.model_description: Agri-OptiCE view-factor ground irradiance, LAI, light-response-curve photosynthesis and biomass simulation
R2529.automated_input_evidence: Hourly weather data for 2019 is collected from the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI)
R2529.actuation_evidence: This alignment ensures consistency between the simulated tracking framework and the on-site system, supporting the realism and future experimental verification of the proposed DLIT and KPT strategies.
R2529.justification: The crop-informed tracking strategies are evaluated only in simulation, driven by historical 2019 SMHI weather data with no live link to the Karrbo tracker. Under the protocol, simulated closed-loop tilt control is not actuation.

R0825.model_description: Polynomial regression models of APV electricity generation and corn yield in a DSS
R0825.automated_input_evidence: the models are calibrated against field experiment data collected from an APV system at Jeollanamdo Agricultural Research and Extension Services
R0825.actuation_evidence: the proposed decision support system can help farmers and system engineers efficiently construct APV systems under various conditions (or environmental factors).
R0825.justification: The regression models were calibrated once on historical field-trial data and are used in a planning and supply-chain DSS that has no streaming input from an installation. Its outputs are design recommendations for people, not actuation.

R1950.model_description: RNN and directed spatio-temporal graph neural network greenhouse temperature predictors
R1950.automated_input_evidence: This study draws on two high-frequency (15-min) data sets collected in Volos (Greece) under the REGACE project.
R1950.actuation_evidence: provide a stepping-stone toward digital twins that jointly optimise crop yield and PV power in agrivoltaic greenhouses
R1950.justification: Data-driven microclimate models are trained and tested offline on historical greenhouse datasets that went through manual imputation, train/test splits and normalisation. The digital twin is mentioned only as a future goal, with no automated ingestion or actuation.

R0344.model_description: Clear-sky direct/diffuse solar radiation model of internal greenhouse radiation under shading
R0344.automated_input_evidence: An analysis was made for the solar radiation available during the year, for cases of completely clear sky and partial cloud, by considering the 15th day of each month.
R0344.actuation_evidence: With this prototype, it is possible to vary the shading inside the greenhouse by panel rotation, in relation to the climatic conditions external to the greenhouse.
R0344.justification: A simple radiation and shading simulation for clear-sky days on the 15th of each month estimates internal radiation for given shading percentages, with no automated input from the prototype. Panels are rotated to keep internal radiation at a set limit (e.g., 400 W m-2), which is rule-based shading control rather than model-driven actuation; the light model is simple enough that it could also be read as borderline.

R2073.model_description: HOMER Pro PV-battery energy simulation (offline sizing and performance model)
R2073.automated_input_evidence: System performance was analyzed using HOMER Pro simulation for energy modeling and Excel-based calculations for technoeconomic analysis.
R2073.actuation_evidence: For example, if TDS rises above 500 ppm, the system increases the pump flow from 8 to 12 L/min.
R2073.justification: The only virtual model is an offline HOMER Pro energy simulation with no live data from the unit. The ESP32 adjusts pump flow and voltage from fixed TDS/pH thresholds and pushes raw sensor values and alerts to a mobile app, so this is threshold control plus monitoring, not a shadow or twin.

R2167.automated_input_evidence: With this module, system data can be remotely monitored and analyzed, allowing farmers to track environmental conditions and energy generation from anywhere.
R2167.actuation_evidence: When soil moisture levels fall below a defined threshold, the system automatically activates the water motor through the L293D motor driver, ensuring timely irrigation.
R2167.justification: An ATmega32P runs threshold-based irrigation and lighting control from soil moisture, rain, LDR and DHT22 sensors, with LCD and IoT display of raw readings. No physics-based or data-driven model of the system is described.

R2468.automated_input_evidence: the ESP32 utilizes its built-in WiFi capability to transmit system data to the Blynk IoT platform.
R2468.actuation_evidence: The architecture employs dual environmental sensing which is illuminance and soil moisture with a threshold-based control strategy embedded within an ESP32 microcontroller.
R2468.justification: The servos track from LDR differences compared with a fixed threshold of 20, and the pump switches at 40% soil moisture. The Blynk dashboard shows raw values and allows manual override; no virtual model is involved, and the miniature prototype was tested.

R2470.model_description: none (COCO-pretrained YOLOv8 apple detector plus rule-based HSV colour index only)
R2470.automated_input_evidence: the collected data were automatically transmitted via the communication module (Cortex M4 processor module) equipped with UMTS (3G) and LTE (4G) standards to a cloud-based platform
R2470.justification: Images are uploaded to the cloud automatically, but the analysis is an object detector plus rule-based colour quantification and statistics, run offline. None of this models how the orchard or PV system behaves, and nothing is actuated.

R2706.model_description: none (rule-based steering: horizontal in rain, sun-tracking above temperature threshold)
R2706.automated_input_evidence: Data from sensors were collected every 30 second and were used to determine the optimal orientation of the trackers of the DAV system.
R2706.actuation_evidence: solar panels were placed in horizontal position during rain events before harvest and solar-tracking position (maximum shading for the trees) [4] when air temperature was above a given threshold.
R2706.justification: Weather-station data automatically steer the trackers in a commercial orchard, but the steering described is rule-based: flat in rain, sun-tracking above a temperature threshold. The text describes no crop, light or energy model in the loop. Confidence is medium because 'optimal orientation' and reference [4] could hint at an undescribed model.

R2710.model_description: none (sensor data acquisition plus post-hoc regression and statistics)
R2710.automated_input_evidence: A database that uses structured query language (SQL) was used to store all the data that is automatically received by the central computer at regular intervals of twenty seconds.
R2710.justification: Wireless sensors log PV current, voltage and temperature to an SQL database automatically. This is raw data acquisition, analysed afterwards with ANOVA and a temperature-voltage regression, with no virtual model of system behaviour and no actuation.

R1623.model_description: geometric solar-incidence model of tracker efficiency and array spacing
R1623.automated_input_evidence: The above designs were used to study the tracking efficiency of agrivoltaics systems using simulation modeling
R1623.justification: An analytical model of the angle of incidence on module planes for several tracker designs computes tracking efficiency and row spacing, with idealised assumptions and no installation data. It goes beyond a bare sun-position formula because it models system geometry, so it is coded digital_model, with medium confidence because the case is borderline.

R1682.model_description: power consumption estimation models and design-phase energy system simulation
R1682.automated_input_evidence: The method for estimating the power consumption of the artificial lighting system considers the experimental measurement of luminosity and different set point values for activating the system.
R1682.actuation_evidence: The artificial lighting system is activated by the computerized intelligent system based on fuzzy logic, which makes decisions based on design premises and monitors the internal luminosity of the greenhouse.
R1682.justification: The greenhouse prototypes run actuators from expert fuzzy rules and set-point thresholds (lux, temperature) with no virtual model in the loop. The only models are offline energy-consumption estimates and design simulations built from recorded data, so the level is digital_model.

R1692.model_description: U-Net deep learning surrogate of raytracer for ground irradiance maps
R1692.automated_input_evidence: we use historical data from the years 2010 to 2019, which were downloaded from the DWD21 open database.
R1692.actuation_evidence: Our surrogate model allows on-the-fly raytracing calculations for edge computing-based PV tracker applications
R1692.justification: A physics-informed surrogate light model was trained and tested on raytracer outputs driven by public historical weather data for the geometry of a real site, with no live data link. Tracker control is mentioned only as a future application.

R1829.automated_input_evidence: The ESP32 continuously acquires raw data from the sensor, applies the regression model, and stores the computed PAR values along with spectral readings onto an SD card for offline analysis
R1829.actuation_evidence: communication capability with smart greenhouse lighting control systems to enable optimized and cost-effective lighting management
R1829.justification: This is a low-cost PAR sensor whose multilinear regression only calibrates spectral channels to PPFD. It does not model system behaviour and only logs data and shows it on a dashboard. Lighting-control integration is mentioned only as a capability and was not demonstrated.

R1969.automated_input_evidence: The LCD will display data from the three sensors.
R1969.actuation_evidence: If the value obtained from the three sensors does not reach the desired value, the controlling system consisting of a pump containing water will water the farm
R1969.justification: In this Arduino prototype, sensors are monitored and irrigation is switched by soil-moisture thresholds, with no virtual model of system behaviour. This is pure sensing plus threshold control, so the level is NA.

R2039.model_description: pvlib PV and crop-irradiance simulation on photogrammetric 3D orchard model
R2039.automated_input_evidence: Simultaneously, real-time sensor data from the hardware is fed back into the digital twin to synchronise the virtual and physical states.
R2039.actuation_evidence: simulation outputs provide the analytical basis for operational decision-making, allowing the user to manually adjust the setpoints of the physical trackers via the dashboard interface.
R2039.justification: Live IoT data (MQTT, InfluxDB) are synchronised into the 3D/pvlib digital environment, and this was validated on a physical solar tracker prototype. Tracker setpoints are changed manually by the user from the dashboard, so the claimed closed loop is human-mediated and the level is digital_shadow, not digital_twin. The truncated text leaves unclear whether live data feed the pvlib simulation itself.

R1141.automated_input_evidence: Based on the solar atlas of the year 2019, the horizontal global irradiance data of the sector were obtained.
R1141.actuation_evidence: It was configured an automatic irrigation two times per day, (6 am and 6 pm) with a duration of 5 minutes each.
R1141.justification: The only calculations are static PV and pump sizing equations using solar-atlas and PVGIS irradiance. They do not model the installation's behaviour. Irrigation on the 20 m2 prototype runs on a fixed time schedule through the Hydrawise controller, which is rule-based control with no virtual model.

R1199.automated_input_evidence: Data from these instruments were aggregated and logged through a remote terminal unit (RTU)
R1199.actuation_evidence: The power output is measured using a WT3000 power analyzer, and the angle is adjusted manually at these crucial times.
R1199.justification: The foldable panels are moved by a time-based single-axis tracking rule built on sun-position geometry, and the shadow-avoiding tilt angles were found empirically and set by hand. Neither counts as a virtual model. The Suncheon testbed data were only logged and analysed.

R1285.model_description: Bifacial Radiance ray-tracing irradiance model and PVWatts DC energy-yield model
R1285.automated_input_evidence: Finally, EPW weather files were imported to simulate two representative days from the measurement period.
R1285.actuation_evidence: The tracking setup is controlled by a PLC that determines the position of the PV modules based on the position of the sun, irradiance level, windspeed, etc.
R1285.justification: The ray-tracing runs used EPW weather files, and PVWatts was applied to measured irradiance as an offline analysis. The cloud database is not described as feeding the models automatically. The PLC tracker runs on sun position and sensor rules with no model in the loop.

R1307.automated_input_evidence: The sensors were connected in parallel to give one integrated signal per PARbar that was recorded by a data logger.
R1307.justification: This is a PAR line-sensor measurement system on a commercial raspberry agrivoltaic farm. The only equation, biomass = intercepted PAR x light use efficiency, is used to work out efficiency from measurements and does not simulate the system. There is no control of any kind.

R1311.model_description: Mechanistic soil-plant-atmosphere energy-balance crop model with raytracing for canopy temperature
R1311.automated_input_evidence: Using only available entries readily measured in AVD systems, it simulates the temperature range of a canopy both in plain field and AVD systems.
R1311.actuation_evidence: More efforts are still required to make the model more robust before trusting it with steering PV panels in commercial settings.
R1311.justification: The model is meant as a decision-support system for steering panels, and its output can go to the grower. However, the text never shows an automated data link to it or the model steering panels automatically, so both criteria are unclear and the lower level applies. The steering policies were compared only in simulation on 2019 Piolenc data, and the model was checked against manual leaf-temperature measurements.

R1359.automated_input_evidence: Original SM records and climatic data have been imported and will be stored and managed in a time series database (InfluxDB) and a connected visualization tool (Grafana).
R1359.justification: Evapotranspiration is worked out offline with Python scripts from declines in measured soil moisture, as a water-balance analysis. FAO-56 potential evapotranspiration serves only as a reference, so neither simulates the installation's behaviour. The data pipeline into InfluxDB and Grafana is monitoring and storage, and there is no control.

R3239.model_description: AVrain geometric rain redistribution model coupled to Hydrus-2D soil water model
R3239.automated_input_evidence: A rain redistribution model (AVrain) was derived from literature elements and theoretical grounds and then validated from experiments in both field and controlled conditions.
R3239.actuation_evidence: during time-variable avoidance strategies that mainly consist in minimizing rain interception by the panels by deciding their titling angle based on wind direction.
R3239.justification: AVrain is a physics-based rain model that was validated offline in R against recorded rain events, with no software link from the site sensors. Panel tilt was set by solar tracking or wind-direction avoidance rules, not by model output. The claim that the model 'allows real-time strategies' is a stated possibility and no architecture for it is described.

R0323.model_description: Ecotect PAR and sunshine-hour distribution simulation model of tracking AV array
R0323.actuation_evidence: When the solar radiation exceeds LSP or is less than 50% of LSP, the system can maximizes the shading area.
R0323.justification: An Ecotect light model of a hypothetical tracking system in Zhangjiakou is simulated using no installation data. The proposed tracking algorithm switches modes by sun-position formulas and light-saturation thresholds rather than by model output, and it was only simulated.

R0352.model_description: Exergy-based greenhouse heat deviation model with real-time energy scheduling optimization
R0352.automated_input_evidence: Input day-ahead and real-time solar irradiance, outdoor temperature, electric loads, thermal loads and other data, and input various parameters required in the calculation model;
R0352.actuation_evidence: so that develop the real-time adjustment plan of energy storage and electric loads.
R0352.justification: A physics-based exergy and scheduling model is applied as an analysis of an actual PV greenhouse case, with inputs entered as data and no software data pipeline described. Its output is an adjustment plan, and no automatic dispatch to storage or loads is described.

R0415.automated_input_evidence: The measured data by each sensor and inverter were stored in a web server by TCP/IP communication, as illustrated in Figure 9.
R0415.actuation_evidence: Smart farming system, in turn, is enabled by the growth environment data from the web server, which provides an automated schedule to control the amount of water supply
R0415.justification: Sensor and inverter data are streamed to a web server for monitoring, but no model of system behavior receives them. Irrigation runs on an automated schedule driven by sensor data with no virtual model, so this is monitoring plus rule-based control.

R0590.actuation_evidence: future work could integrate a temperature sensor, fan and/or a motor to control air inflow into the greenhouse box to regulate its temperature using an Arduino microcontroller
R0590.justification: The parametric OpenSCAD script and cost calculations describe geometry and material cost, not the behavior of light, energy, crop, microclimate or water. Sensor-based automation appears only as future work, and masses come from Cura estimates, with no built unit reported.

R0700.model_description: 2D radiation view-factor model with Perez transposition and PVWatts energy model
R0700.automated_input_evidence: the diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) and direct normal irradiance (DNI) inputs are taken from the TMY pvgis database
R0700.justification: A design webtool runs radiation and energy models on typical-year PVGIS weather, with results precomputed offline into an SQL database. It has no link to any specific installation and no actuation.

R0804.model_description: unspecified mathematical crop growth and irrigation models in a control center (concept only)
R0804.automated_input_evidence: The obtained data are sent to the control center, where they are entered into mathematical models of growth, irrigation, etc.
R0804.actuation_evidence: the control system determines the sections and irrigation rates. Railer receives the necessary data from the control system (section, volume) and transmits the results in real time.
R0804.justification: The concept sends sensor data to growth and irrigation models in a control center, but the models are only named, and it is unclear whether model outputs drive the railer without people, since the complex is 'remotely controlled' and panel rotation follows fixed rules. Following the lower-level rule I coded a designed digital shadow; nothing was built, so no level is demonstrated.

R0838.model_description: none (CNN leaf-disease image classifier is not a virtual model)
R0838.automated_input_evidence: These captured data will be send to the controller to process and take appropriate action.
R0838.actuation_evidence: Fan will be turned on for ventilation or cooling when the sensed temperature value is greater than the threshold value
R0838.justification: A small Raspberry Pi greenhouse prototype runs threshold-based actuators, a Blynk dashboard and a CNN disease classifier; it has no model of the system's behavior. The vague mentions of 'ML algorithms' and growth-rate prediction are never specified or shown, so this is NA at both levels.

R0909.model_description: crop models plus AI steering algorithm; Penman-Monteith ETo estimation per modality
R0909.automated_input_evidence: The solar panels are oriented using information collected from environmental and plant sensors.
