R0909.actuation_evidence: we propose to use an artificial intelligence to pilot the orientation of solar panels using environmental and plant indicators derived from both sensors and crop models.
R0909.justification: The design is a sensor- and crop-model-driven AI that steers the tracker panels, which is a digital twin. But the AI loop is only a 'conceptual algorithm' said to be under evaluation at Tresserre with no results; the reported Piolenc results come from a fixed afternoon-shading policy, plus Penman-Monteith ETo computed offline from measured data (a digital model at most).

R1076.model_description: photosynthesis light-response model; annual energy and water balance model of the tunnel
R1076.automated_input_evidence: These systems allow for continuous recording of data (for example in the cloud), which are subsequently subject to automatic analysis
R1076.actuation_evidence: Based on the estimated parameter values, a method of controlling the climatic conditions in the tunnel was proposed.
R1076.justification: The concept paper uses a photosynthesis-rate model and energy/water balance analyses across four climates; the control appears to rely on thresholds derived offline from the model, and the text does not show live installation data reaching a model. The packet is truncated before the chapters on control algorithms and tunnel constructions, which could change the coding, so I chose the lower level.

R1084.model_description: Ladybug Tools/Radiance irradiance simulation of ground-level shading under the PV array
R1084.automated_input_evidence: The model used the Fort Collins-Loveland Municipal Airport TMY3 file.
R1084.actuation_evidence: irrigation was supplied 3 times a day for 15-minute intervals at 8:00, 12:00, and 16:00
R1084.justification: Ground irradiance was simulated with a Radiance-based model driven by a typical-year weather file, while microclimate data were logged separately by HOBO loggers. There is no automated link to the model and no model-driven actuation, so this is a digital model.

R1134.model_description: planned ML crop-yield prediction model under panel coverage; not yet built
R1134.automated_input_evidence: A framework is proposed to exploit Internet of Things (IoT) concepts, with a sensor network to collect data on the field merged with sensor fusion
R1134.justification: Despite the 'digital twin' title, the work reports only lysimeter shading experiments whose sensor data were logged to build a future ML yield model; no model is built, and it is unclear whether a live data link is intended. The designed level is therefore digital model (the lower level), and the only demonstrated data flow is sensing and data acquisition (NA).

R2177.model_description: monofacial/bifacial radiation model used in rule- and optimization-based tilt control
R2177.automated_input_evidence: We compare different variants of the proposed schemes across multiple crop light requirements and DC/AC ratios through 384 simulations.
R2177.actuation_evidence: a proactive, model-based control algorithm that determines panel tilt angles based on weather forecasts while respecting constraints such as inverter capacity
R2177.justification: A radiation model drives tilt-angle control, but its inputs are weather forecasts and the study is a set of simulations, with no automated data link to a specific installation. The full text could show that the reactive deficit-correction strategy uses measured installation data, which would raise the designed level.

R2220.model_description: U-Net++ segmentation, EfficientNet-B3 stress classifier, CNN growth-trait regressor (image-based)
R2220.automated_input_evidence: Shading and irrigation control relied on monitored plant vigor assessed using a U-Net++ implementation for canopy segmentation, an EfficientNet-B3 implementation for stress differentiation
R2220.actuation_evidence: This method implemented the control of cucumber plant shading and irrigation in real time using monitored plant vigor.
R2220.justification: The closed loop is driven by CNN image segmentation, classification and trait estimation, which are perception tools rather than models of system behavior, and the yield results are described as simulated. Whether any crop or microclimate model sits in the control loop cannot be told from the abstract, so the lower level is chosen.

R2234.model_description: solar-trajectory shadow analysis algorithm and minute-level dynamic PV power generation model
R2234.automated_input_evidence: a minute-level precision dynamic photovoltaic power generation model that integrates real-time meteorological data to achieve continuous output power evaluation and system performance monitoring
R2234.actuation_evidence: providing quantitative decision support for agrivoltaic system design
R2234.justification: Shadow and PV power models feed a design-stage multi-objective optimization. The abstract mentions real-time meteorological data but does not say whether they come automatically from a specific installation, so the lower level is chosen.

R2254.model_description: mathematical light/power model with mixed-integer tilt optimization
R2254.automated_input_evidence: the results of numerical simulations are reported and discussed, using real-world data based on an existing agrivoltaic plant in Southern Italy.
R2254.actuation_evidence: a novel optimization-based approach for automatically controlling the balance between the crops’ light exposure and the power generation
R2254.justification: An optimization model is designed to set tilt angles automatically, but it is evaluated only in numerical simulation on plant data used offline, with no automated data link. Since there is no automated input, the level stays at digital model even though control is automated in simulation.

R2264.model_description: multiple linear regression and tree-based ensemble crop yield-response models
R2264.automated_input_evidence: This study evaluates yield responses across a global dataset of 546 observations from 66 studies, including agrivoltaic, shading, and agroforestry systems.
R2264.justification: This is a meta-analysis that builds data-driven models of crop yield response to shading from literature data. There is no link to an installation and no actuation.

R2286.automated_input_evidence: A comprehensive network of over 80 sensors is being deployed across the site to monitor environmental, agricultural, and PV variables in real-time.
R2286.justification: A pilot sensor network for monitoring only, with no virtual model described.

R2288.automated_input_evidence: which provides the foundation for future integration with predictive models and energy-use optimization strategies.
R2288.actuation_evidence: while also automating irrigation based on sensor feedback.
R2288.justification: Pilot greenhouse monitoring with irrigation automated by sensor feedback through programmable logic. Predictive models are explicitly left for future work.

R2293.automated_input_evidence: data collection and transmission are carried out via ZigBee wireless communication to achieve system data monitoring and real-time control.
R2293.actuation_evidence: to achieve system data monitoring and real-time control
R2293.justification: A microcontroller and ZigBee monitoring and control system with no virtual model. Control is presumably rule-based on sensor readings.

R2299.actuation_evidence: The generated solar power was utilized to operate LED lights for supplemental illumination during low-light conditions
R2299.justification: A physical agrivoltaic trellis with automated LED lighting under low-light conditions, which is threshold-based. The term 'agrovoltaic model' refers to the system concept, not a virtual model.

R2332.actuation_evidence: A low-cost photovoltaic (PV)-powered microclimate control system was deployed to regulate temperature, humidity, and vapor pressure deficit while sustaining electricity generation.
R2332.justification: An empirical season-long comparison of controlled and uncontrolled PV greenhouses. The microclimate control appears to be set-point control from sensors, with no virtual model described.

R2877.automated_input_evidence: Microclimate was monitored with an IoT sensor network (air and soil temperature, humidity, PAR)
R2877.actuation_evidence: Key engineering aspects include strong support structures, effective shading, and integrated monitoring for data-driven control.
R2877.justification: A hortivoltaic pilot with IoT microclimate monitoring and descriptive results. No virtual model or actuation is described.

R2806.model_description: unspecified optimization algorithm for automated PV module movement (planned)
R2806.automated_input_evidence: During the project, the PV performance in terms of efficiency and electricity production will be continuously monitored.
R2806.actuation_evidence: The movement of the PV modules will be automated and controlled through customizable control and management logic, aiming at obtaining an optimal trade-off condition between crop and energy yields.
R2806.justification: A planned project with automated movable PV modules run by an optimization algorithm. Whether that algorithm uses a light, crop or energy model fed by monitoring data is not stated, so the lower level is chosen.

R2485.model_description: yield projection model for 10-year shade-factor scenarios
R2485.automated_input_evidence: Model projections suggest that agrivoltaic systems designed with 20–25 % shade factors could limit 10-year yield reductions to approximately 20 %.
R2485.justification: A four-year field trial under fixed panels with an offline yield projection model. There is no automated data link and no actuation.

R2549.model_description: three-layer PV-battery capacity, scheduling and real-time control optimization model
R2549.automated_input_evidence: a supply–demand matching coefficient was developed and applied to a year-long tomato cultivation experiment, quantifying significant mismatches.
R2549.actuation_evidence: systematically coordinating capacity design, weekly scheduling, and real-time control with growth stages
R2549.justification: An optimization framework built from experimental data used offline and evaluated by comparative economic results. Whether the real-time control layer runs on live greenhouse data and actuators is not stated.

R2562.model_description: solar geometry and ray-tracing real-time greenhouse shadow prediction model
R2562.automated_input_evidence: served as the basis for a real-time model predicting greenhouse shadows by integrating solar geometry and ray-tracing algorithms
R2562.actuation_evidence: this study developed a dynamic tracking photovoltaic greenhouse (TPVG) system
R2562.justification: A physical tracking PV greenhouse with a ray-tracing shadow model. The abstract does not say whether the model receives automated installation data or drives tracker actuation, so the lower level is chosen.

R2591.automated_input_evidence: Extensive experiments on real agricultural vision benchmarks and agrivoltaic shadow variants demonstrate that PrivAgriVolt improves stress recognition and segmentation under PV shading
R2591.justification: A federated image classification and segmentation framework for crop stress, evaluated on benchmarks. It is an image classifier, not a model of system behavior.

R2624.model_description: empirical enthalpy-photosynthetic rate relationship used to set regulation thresholds
R2624.actuation_evidence: Based on the relationship between enthalpy and photosynthetic rate, a dynamic regulation strategy was proposed using the critical enthalpy value as a threshold.
R2624.justification: The regulation strategy is threshold-based, using a critical enthalpy value derived from greenhouse measurements. Whether a crop or energy model beyond this empirical relation exists cannot be told from the abstract.

R2662.model_description: simulation models of PV-induced microclimate, soil-water dynamics and energy production
R2662.automated_input_evidence: integrates an actively controlled photovoltaic layer with distributed environmental sensing, energy-aware irrigation scheduling, and real-time flow-based leak detection.
R2662.actuation_evidence: Simulation results demonstrate that the dynamic shading algorithm mitigates peak air temperatures by 3–4°C
R2662.justification: A proposed cyber-physical architecture evaluated only in simulation. The abstract does not say whether live sensor data feed the microclimate, soil-water and energy models or whether those models drive shading and irrigation, so the lower level is chosen.

R2695.model_description: PVsyst PV energy and economic performance simulation
R2695.automated_input_evidence: The system's performance and economic viability were assessed with PVsyst software.
R2695.actuation_evidence: Only the Building Integrated Photovoltaic greenhouse was able to consistently maintain a suitable environment (temperature ≤25 °C, humidity ≥65%) after system activation.
R2695.justification: Experimental greenhouses with real-time sensor monitoring and an environmental control system that is not model-based. The only virtual model is an offline PVsyst assessment.

R0200.model_description: unspecified analysis of OPV greenhouse crop growth and electricity
R0200.justification: The one-sentence abstract says OPV is analysed for greenhouse use but does not say whether a light, crop or energy model is used. Following the unclear rule the lower level NA is chosen; the full text could show an offline model (digital_model).

R0268.actuation_evidence: A large increase in transmitted radiation was achieved by restricting solar tracking around midday
R0268.justification: Field experiment comparing fixed and tracking panels under fixed orientation policies, with lettuce growth measured; no virtual model is described. Tracker actuation follows rule-based policies, not model outputs.

R3144.actuation_evidence: flexible solar panels/thin films which are programmed to deploy automatically, based on measured sunlight at any given time.
R3144.justification: A folding PV screen that deploys directly from measured sunlight is sensor-driven control with no virtual model. The abstract presents it as a concept with no reported prototype results.

R0367.model_description: PV power prediction simulation used offline to tune fuzzy MPPT controller
R0367.automated_input_evidence: Calculations and simulation of power prediction algorithm were carried out for obtaining the suitable parameters and duty cycle of the fuzzy control algorithm
R0367.actuation_evidence: the fuzzy control algorithm, to modulate output power in real-time
R0367.justification: A PV power simulation is used offline to set fuzzy MPPT parameters. The real-time loop is a rule-based fuzzy controller acting on measurements, not a virtual model fed by installation data.

R0462.model_description: MATLAB/Simulink PV array and MPPT simulation model
R0462.automated_input_evidence: Through the MPPT modelling and simulation in MATLAB/Simulink and the corresponding circuit test
R0462.actuation_evidence: proposes a new variable-step conductance increment method to track the maximum power point
R0462.justification: A Simulink PV/MPPT model is run offline, and the MPPT itself is a rule-based incremental-conductance controller tested on a circuit. No installation data feed a model.

R0490.model_description: reduced-order ray-tracing light model with genomic machine-learning optimizer
R0490.automated_input_evidence: Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the results, with the overall goal being to provide a computational framework to rapidly design and deploy complex APV systems.
R0490.justification: Despite the 'digital twin' label, this is a design-stage ray-tracing and optimization framework run on numerical examples. No installation data feed it and it drives no actuators.

R0497.actuation_evidence: as per scheduled operations of airflow, photosynthetically active radiation for improved photosynthesis, climate control, and backup battery energy source
R0497.justification: A hardware PV power-optimizer prototype that uses MPPT and scheduled loads. No virtual model of system behavior is described, and control is rule- or schedule-based.

R0524.actuation_evidence: in the establishment of intelligent control systems for greenhouses in the temperature, brightness, gas concentration and other parameters to do further regulation
R0524.justification: Describes sun tracking and greenhouse parameter regulation by 'intelligent' equipment, with no virtual model named. No implementation results are reported.

R0531.actuation_evidence: Microcontroller ATmega 2560 hardware-based coordinated, unified control and monitoring architecture is developed to manage the PV-GH internal parameters within defined boundary conditions.
R0531.justification: A microcontroller automation architecture keeps greenhouse parameters within set boundary conditions, which is threshold or rule-based control. No virtual model is involved.

R0534.model_description: CFD simulation of greenhouse airflow and temperature
R0534.automated_input_evidence: simulation of the fluid dynamics and temperature, and the functional design and system behavior
R0534.actuation_evidence: ventilation, horizontal air flow (HAF) fan, and exhaust fan can be utilized to maintain temperature and humidity in the greenhouse in a range of optimum values
R0534.justification: A design-stage CFD model of the greenhouse microclimate is not linked to sensor data. The IoT monitoring goes to users' phones, and fan control to keep values in a range is rule-based.

R0621.model_description: none; geostatistical kriging maps of measured PPFD
R0621.automated_input_evidence: Following semivariogram and kriging approach, spatial variation of PPFD and DLI was quantified within the AVS.
R0621.justification: A measurement study of light in a 105 kWp AVS that uses kriging only to interpolate measured PPFD; there is no behavioral model of the system. Nothing is actuated or streamed to a model.

R0648.model_description: data-driven crop yield and monetary performance estimation model in DSS
R0648.automated_input_evidence: the real-time monitoring data is used as an input of the DSS system for performance estimation of an APV system in terms of production yields
R0648.actuation_evidence: The proposed DSS is devised to provide a mobile application service, satellite image processing, real-time data monitoring, and performance estimation.
R0648.justification: Real-time monitoring data from an actual APV system feed a performance-estimation model whose outputs go to farmers through a DSS, with no actuation. Whether the live data link actually ran, rather than offline validation with field data, needs the full text to confirm.

R0652.model_description: geometric ray-tracing light model with genomic optimization of greenhouse design
R0652.automated_input_evidence: Representative numerical examples are provided. The framework can be used to generate tailored, temporal and location-specific greenhouse designs.
R0652.justification: Despite the 'digital-twin' title, this is a ray-tracing design and optimization tool run on numerical examples. It has no installation data input and no actuation.

R0803.model_description: theoretical PV yield estimate from solar explorer web tool
R0803.automated_input_evidence: data stored on the web platforms of PV systems providers, compare the actual annual production of each greenhouse with the theoretical annual production estimated with the solar explorer web tool
R0803.justification: Measured production from two operating PV greenhouses is retrieved and compared after the fact with theoretical estimates from a web tool. The model gets no automated installation input and drives nothing.

R0867.automated_input_evidence: To measure the temperature, humidity, moisture, and the PV panel output voltage, current a microcontroller-based data logger is designed.
R0867.justification: A microcontroller data logger on an experimental prototype records microclimate and PV data for later analysis. This is pure sensing with no virtual model.

R0889.model_description: PV energy-harvesting and irrigation-demand simulation considering rainfall and shading
R0889.automated_input_evidence: The simulation part of the study considers the rainy condition of the location to understand the impact on the energy harvesting of the system.
R0889.actuation_evidence: The designed system can automatically turn on the irrigation based on the sensor data and can be controlled and monitored remotely.
R0889.justification: An offline design simulation sizes PV and irrigation, while irrigation switching is driven directly by sensor data with no model in the loop. The model therefore stays a digital model.

R0901.automated_input_evidence: the solar output electrical parameters voltage and current are measured hourly using data logger of Arduino
R0901.justification: A small vertical agrivoltaic prototype with an Arduino data logger and automated irrigation, with no virtual model described. Any irrigation automation is rule- or sensor-based.

R0921.automated_input_evidence: soil characteristics such as moisture, NPK content, electrical conductivity and pH were monitored using IoT technology for real-time tracking
R0921.justification: A pilot crop trial with IoT soil monitoring only, with no model and no actuation. This is raw-data monitoring.

R3082.model_description: none; AGV cleaning-robot kinematic model, not an agrivoltaic subsystem
R3082.automated_input_evidence: the carrier kinetics and kinematics are modeled and validated through simulations
R3082.actuation_evidence: position and trajectory controllers are designed and simulations are presented
R3082.justification: The only model describes a cleaning robot's dynamics, not the light, PV energy, crop, microclimate or water behavior of the agrivoltaic system. Its controllers are tested only in simulation at an initial-design stage.

R0970.automated_input_evidence: This paper presents a flexible, customizable, reliable sensor node and open platform.
R0970.justification: An open-platform sensor node for data acquisition; actuation and ML appear only as general background. No virtual model is developed.

R1035.automated_input_evidence: two testbeds were designed and a series of experiments in PA was performed
R1035.justification: Testbed experiments on wireless signal interference for solar insecticidal lamps in PV agriculture. There is no model of system behavior and no actuation.

R1105.model_description: PV generation and shading simulations for single-axis tracking strategies
R1105.actuation_evidence: During the production season, the dynamic PV systems switch to the shadow-free mode to ensure the photosynthesis of crops within the CSGs.
R1105.justification: Simulations of tracking strategies are paired with experiments and a large-scale installation. The trackers run fixed strategies and switch modes by season (rule-based), and no model fed by installation data is described.

R1108.model_description: unspecified technical-economic analysis of greenhouse PV
R1108.justification: The very short abstract describes a techno-economic feasibility analysis without saying whether a PV yield model is used. The lower level NA is chosen; the full text could show an offline energy model (digital_model).

R1149.model_description: AI predictive model only planned; current fertigation logic not described
R1149.automated_input_evidence: SolarFertigation can monitor and optimize fertigation autonomously, based on the analysis of data collected through the cloud.
R1149.actuation_evidence: the central unit, which enables the precise deployment and distribution of water and fertilizers in different areas of the agricultural field
R1149.justification: Cloud data drive autonomous fertigation, but the AI predictive model is only an infrastructure goal, and the current decision logic (likely rule-based) is not described. The lower level is chosen, and the full text could show a model in the loop (shadow or twin).

R1202.model_description: simplified agrivoltaic transparency model in graphical interface
R1202.automated_input_evidence: estimate the appropriate transparency level of a solar greenhouse covers according to the characteristics of the crop and the location, using a simplified agrivoltaic model
R1202.justification: A portable design tool runs a simplified agrivoltaic model on crop and location inputs, not on data from an installation. 'Real-time' here refers to computation speed, not sensor input.

R1204.model_description: possible PV layout generation and water-use estimates; not specified
R1204.automated_input_evidence: transmitting the data wirelessly to a centralized database for processing and analysis
R1204.actuation_evidence: Farmers can remotely access vital information through a user-friendly web interface, monitor crop parameters, track changes, and receive alerts about irrigation needs.
R1204.justification: Sensor data stream to a database for dashboards and irrigation alerts, and irrigation is 'automated' per the title, which implies threshold control. Whether a PV or water model exists is unclear, so the lower level NA is chosen.

R1211.model_description: lighting simulation model for design; AI greenhouse controller of unclear type
R1211.automated_input_evidence: A sensor network monitors indoor environmental variables, and a weather station monitors outdoor environmental variables.
R1211.actuation_evidence: A computational system based on artificial intelligence is responsible for the autonomous control of the greenhouses.
R1211.justification: The lighting system was designed with an offline simulation model, while the AI controller that autonomously runs the sensor-equipped greenhouses is not described as a model of system behavior. The lower level is chosen, and the full text could show a model-based closed loop.

R1231.model_description: none; GRU-AdaBoost classifier of crop and panel condition
R1231.automated_input_evidence: The proposed model focuses on energy-efficient data aggregation and classification for monitoring agrovoltaics using real-time data.
R1231.justification: The ML component classifies sensor data into crop-health and panel-condition states and does not model system behavior. WSN data aggregation for monitoring is otherwise pure data acquisition.

R2994.automated_input_evidence: This study investigates the implementation of Fluorescent Solar Concentrators (FSC) in greenhouse with an IoT-based monitoring system as an alternative agro-shade material.
R2994.actuation_evidence: A small greenhouse with roofing integrated with FSC was constructed to generate power for the IoT monitoring system and control environmental variables like temperature, humidity, and light intensity.
R2994.justification: An FSC-roofed greenhouse prototype with IoT monitoring and environmental control, with no virtual model described. Any control is sensor- or rule-based.

R1279.automated_input_evidence: The prototype uses IoT, 3D printing, and commercial components.
R1279.actuation_evidence: Experiments had been conducted to enhance light-dependent resistor (LDR) accuracy for tracking, exploring shielding and tradeoffs.
R1279.justification: A solar-tree prototype whose tracking is driven directly by LDR sensors, which is sensor-based control with no virtual model. This is level NA.

R1367.model_description: GWO-BP neural network greenhouse temperature forecaster; architectural PV layout model
R1367.automated_input_evidence: employing LoRa modules for information transmission from the collection terminal and enabling remote interaction with the upper computer through the NB-IoT module
R1367.actuation_evidence: we introduce an improved APSO-optimized fuzzy PID algorithm (APSO-FUZZY-PID) and compare its control effects with two other temperature control models
R1367.justification: A data-driven temperature forecaster exists but is evaluated only in MATLAB simulation, with no stated live link from the LoRa/NB-IoT monitoring system. Control is fuzzy PID feedback with no model in the loop.

R1384.model_description: possible empirical outdoor-to-indoor irradiance correlation used for light dimming
R1384.automated_input_evidence: The Internet of Things (IoT) technology was integrated into the system to remotely monitor the variations in ambient light, solar irradiance, and energy consumption
R1384.actuation_evidence: An adaptive control algorithm based on the correlation of outdoor solar irradiance and the ambient light inside the solar greenhouse was developed to dynamically adjust the illuminance
R1384.justification: The dimming controller uses a light correlation, and the abstract does not show whether that is a light-transmission model or just a sensor-driven rule. Treated as sensor-driven control (NA), with low confidence.

R1397.actuation_evidence: The experimental setup includes a solar-powered greenhouse with IoT-controlled micro-climate management to ensure optimal growing conditions.
R1397.justification: The CNN models count chili crops from images, which makes them image classifiers rather than models of system behavior. The IoT microclimate control has no virtual model described.

R1443.model_description: machine learning analytics with multi-objective optimization for louvre angle
R1443.automated_input_evidence: The proposed DSS integrates and synchronizes multi-sensor data acquisition, data quality management, machine learning and analytics, and multi-objective optimization
R1443.actuation_evidence: multi-objective optimization for adaptive control of the louvre to a specified angle position
R1443.justification: The architecture is designed as a closed loop: sensor data feed ML/optimization models that set louvre angles in real time. Implementation and simulation are ongoing, so nothing is demonstrated.

R1452.actuation_evidence: automatically adjust the tilt angle of the PV modules according to the sun’s altitude and the crop growth stage
R1452.justification: Tilt is set by sun altitude and crop-stage rules, which are sun-position plus rule-based control with no virtual model. An 8 kW prototype was tested.

R1531.automated_input_evidence: Real-time data collection was performed using an IoT platform integrated with an ESP32 microcontroller and visualized through the Blynk dashboard
R1531.justification: This is pure IoT sensing with a raw-data dashboard on a fixed-tilt prototype. No model and no actuation are described.

R1540.model_description: possible PAR shading and crop evapotranspiration analysis, offline
R1540.actuation_evidence: integrating conventional solar tracking with dual-use water systems for irrigation and module cleaning
R1540.justification: The system uses conventional tracking plus combined irrigation and cleaning, with 6 months of operation. The abstract does not say whether the PAR/evapotranspiration analysis is model-based, so the lower level is chosen.

R1541.model_description: none (MILP IoT gateway placement optimization, not system behavior)
R1541.justification: The MILP optimizes where communication gateways go and does not represent light, energy, crop, microclimate, or water behavior. It is a planning analysis, not an implemented system.

R1618.model_description: climate-adaptive crop model with irrigation and nutrient optimization
R1618.automated_input_evidence: Soil moisture, crop status, and environmental data are continuously monitored to assist climate-adaptive crop modeling, optimal irrigation scheduling
R1618.actuation_evidence: the nutrient optimization module, which dynamically regulates fertilizer supply based on information from soil nutrient sensor readings and crop growth phases
R1618.justification: A crop model is designed to receive continuously monitored sensor data, but the abstract does not say whether model outputs drive fertilizer or irrigation actuators. Validation is MATLAB simulation plus vague case studies.

R1626.automated_input_evidence: Real-time monitoring and control of environmental and operational variables are achieved through a wireless interface using NI myRIO-1900 and LabVIEW, enabling remote supervision
R1626.actuation_evidence: The proposed agrivoltaic system features a solar tracking mechanism controlled by a proportional-integral (PI) controller
R1626.justification: PI feedback tracking and remote monitoring and supervision run on a built prototype. No virtual model of system behavior is described.

R1629.actuation_evidence: An Arduino-based control and monitoring is implemented to have an automatic horizontal with tilt adjustment in agrivoltaic system.
R1629.justification: LDR-based tracking and soil-moisture-regulated irrigation are sensor-driven control. The rest is raw monitoring, and no virtual model is described.

R1636.actuation_evidence: The laboratory integrates modern photovoltaic technologies, sensor networks, IoT platforms, and automated irrigation systems
R1636.justification: This is a conceptual laboratory framework with sensors, IoT, and automated irrigation, and no virtual model is described. The full text might include a shading optimization model.

R1637.model_description: greenhouse irradiance distribution model validated against measurements
R1637.automated_input_evidence: The experimental phase also served as a benchmark for validating the irradiance distribution simulation.
R1637.actuation_evidence: dynamic photovoltaic panels were integrated in a Nordic greenhouse and controlled based on incoming irradiance
R1637.justification: The irradiance model was developed in parallel and validated offline against experimental data. Panel control responds to measured irradiance, and the model is not shown in the loop.

R1638.model_description: none (Conv1D-SNN sensor data classifier for transmission)
R1638.justification: The SNN classifies sensor data to cut redundant wireless transmission. It does not model the behavior of the agrivoltaic system.

R1711.model_description: monitoring and analytics platform; model content unspecified
R1711.automated_input_evidence: to offer operators in this new sector a platform as a tool to have a global view of the system
R1711.justification: The platform monitors and analyses system parameters for operators. The abstract does not show whether the analytics include a behavioral model, so the lower level is chosen.

R1722.model_description: block-cooling greenhouse energy and microclimate model with PV-battery system
R1722.actuation_evidence: decoupled temperature and humidity control is proposed and realised via the proportion-integration-differentiation (PID) controller
R1722.justification: A cooling-load and energy model is evaluated with PID/PI controllers in simulation, with no automated link to a specific installation. Cooling scheduling is rule-based by irradiance level.

R1762.model_description: cloud AI predictive analysis of greenhouse conditions
R1762.automated_input_evidence: the cyber domain processes data via artificial intelligence and cloud services
R1762.actuation_evidence: facilitate real-time monitoring, predictive analysis, and dynamic control of greenhouse conditions
R1762.justification: Sensor data reach cloud AI predictive analysis on the Savona prototype. The abstract does not say whether control is automatic from the model or goes through the GUI user, so the lower level is chosen.

R1800.justification: This is a proposed micro-needle impedance sensor for plant monitoring, so it is pure sensing. No model or actuation is described.

R1811.model_description: tracking logic maximizing agro-energy yield; nature unspecified
R1811.automated_input_evidence: A low cost dedicated monitoring system is going to be implemented in order to store data related to indoor and outdoor sensor measurements.
R1811.actuation_evidence: The proposal introduces a tracking system based on a logic designed to maximize the agro-energy yield of the agrivoltaic system.
R1811.justification: This is a project proposal with tracking logic and planned data storage. The abstract does not say whether the tracking logic is rule-based or model-based, so the lower level is chosen.

R1814.model_description: first-principles multi-objective PV greenhouse model: energy, yield, water, quality, economics
R1814.automated_input_evidence: Empirical validation is conducted over a 97-day tomato crop cycle in a semi-arid, off-grid PVGH.
R1814.actuation_evidence: Implemented as a low-cost digital twin, the framework supports adaptive, quality-aware greenhouse control
R1814.justification: A field-validated first-principles model exists, but the abstract does not show automated data flow or model-driven actuation. The authors' digital twin label is not taken as evidence.

R1823.model_description: dynamic climate-adaptive crop model with water management optimization
R1823.automated_input_evidence: Real-time data analytics is employed to improve water conservation, crop health prediction, and energy efficiency.
R1823.justification: An IoT framework is designed to feed real-time sensor data to a dynamic crop model, with no stated automatic actuation. The demonstration is in MATLAB, with vague case studies.

R2900.model_description: exploratory ML (PCA, K-means) for strawberry yield prediction
R2900.automated_input_evidence: Environmental parameters were monitored at 15 minute intervals, while strawberry production data were collected as daily aggregates.
R2900.justification: This is an offline analysis of logged monitoring data from an AVS. PCA and clustering are descriptive, and whether a yield prediction model was actually built is unclear, so the lower level is chosen.

R1871.model_description: simulation model of PV supply, DC bus and irrigation load
R1871.actuation_evidence: presents simulation-based tests of the modified MPPT and coupled non-linear digital irrigation control system
R1871.justification: The MPPT and irrigation controllers are tested only against a simulation model, with no automated input from the installation. The controllers are feedback control, not model-driven.

R1896.actuation_evidence: By selectively controlling panel deployment during midday peaks, solar power generation is maximized at times of reduced plant photosynthetic efficiency.
R1896.justification: Retractable panels are deployed on a time-of-day schedule (11 a.m. to 2 p.m.), which is rule-based. The plant-factory pilot test has no virtual model.

R1932.model_description: cloud fertigation automation models; rule-based or agronomic model unclear
R1932.automated_input_evidence: It enables precise, adaptive management of fertigation processes based on real-time environmental, agronomic, and operational data
R1932.actuation_evidence: advanced automation models that adjust fertigation schedules dynamically according to crop phenology, weather conditions, soil characteristics, topography, and machine status
R1932.justification: Real-time data reach a cloud platform whose automation models adjust fertigation schedules. The abstract does not say whether these are behavioral models or schedule rules, so the lower level is chosen, and only LoRaWAN coverage was validated in the field.

R2062.model_description: MPC with PV power, shading factor and crop yield models
R2062.automated_input_evidence: dynamically adjusts panel positions in real time to maximize power production and crop yield given solar irradiance and ambient temperature measurements
R2062.actuation_evidence: we propose a model predictive control (MPC) approach to dual-axis agrivoltaic panel tracking control
R2062.justification: As designed, MPC uses measurements and a model to set panel positions automatically. It is evaluated only in simulated case studies, which do not count as a demonstration.

R2108.automated_input_evidence: IoT based sensors, which monitor soil moisture, weather data, and crop conditions in real time
R2108.actuation_evidence: A smart irrigation mechanism uses this data to automate water distribution
R2108.justification: Irrigation is automated directly from sensor data, with no virtual model described. The project is framed as a design aim.

R2171.model_description: unspecified AI controller for vertical farming system
R2171.actuation_evidence: fully automated, and AI-controlled Outdoor Agrivoltaic Vertical Farming (OAVF) system
R2171.justification: The proposal claims AI control, but the abstract describes no model, data flow, or actuation logic, so the lower level is chosen.

R2824.actuation_evidence: we report an automated foldable organic PV (OPV) system designed to function as a dynamic alternative to conventional shade nets
R2824.justification: The foldable OPV is deployed automatically on a set duration schedule, with no virtual model in the loop. It was tested in a melon greenhouse.

R2176.model_description: data-driven irrigation module, PV cleaning economic model, tilt management module
R2176.automated_input_evidence: integrates multi-parameter field monitoring, edge and cloud-based data management, environmental and crop monitoring, a data-driven irrigation module
R2176.actuation_evidence: the proposed system transforms real-time field observations into operational recommendations for irrigation, PV operation, and economic management
R2176.justification: The platform is designed to feed live field data into models whose outputs are recommendations for people. The irrigation module was assessed retrospectively and the other modules were not validated, so whether the live model feed ran is unclear and the lower level is chosen.

R2517.model_description: shading simulation and PV performance models validated against field measurements
R2517.automated_input_evidence: validating modeling approaches with experimental data
R2517.actuation_evidence: This latter aspect is also optimized by the possibility of manually adjust the tilt of the panels when needed due to agricultural management requirements.
R2517.justification: The shading and PV simulations are run offline and checked against field data from two experimental APV sites. Datalogger files are uploaded daily to a cloud server, but nothing shows them feeding a model automatically, and panel tilt is adjusted by hand.

R2529.model_description: Agri-OptiCE view-factor ground irradiance, LAI, light-response-curve photosynthesis and biomass simulation
R2529.automated_input_evidence: Hourly weather data for 2019 is collected from the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI)
R2529.actuation_evidence: supporting the realism and future experimental verification of the proposed DLIT and KPT strategies
R2529.justification: The crop-informed tracking strategies are tested only in a simulation driven by historical public SMHI weather data, with no data link to the Karrbo tracker. Tilt control is a simulated closed loop, so it counts neither as actuation nor as a demonstration, and no real-time data architecture is described.

R0825.model_description: polynomial regression models of PV electricity generation and corn yield
R0825.automated_input_evidence: Field experiment data provided by the APV system at Jeollanamdo Agricultural Research and Extension Services in South Korea were utilized.
R0825.actuation_evidence: the proposed decision support system can help farmers and system engineers efficiently construct APV systems under various conditions
R0825.justification: Regression models fitted offline to field data from a test APV system feed a mobile decision support tool for siting and supply-chain design. There is no automated data link to an installation and no actuation; the outputs go to planners.

R1950.model_description: RNN and spatio-temporal graph neural network greenhouse temperature forecasters
R1950.automated_input_evidence: This study draws on two high-frequency (15-min) data sets collected in Volos (Greece) under the REGACE project.
R1950.actuation_evidence: provide a stepping-stone toward digital twins that jointly optimise crop yield and PV power in agrivoltaic greenhouses
R1950.justification: Data-driven microclimate models are trained and tested offline on historical greenhouse datasets, and the authors present this only as a step toward a digital twin. No automated data pipeline or actuation is described.

R0344.model_description: clear-sky solar radiation and shading-transmittance calculation of greenhouse internal radiation
R0344.automated_input_evidence: For this simulation, the 15th of each month in clear sky conditions was considered (Figure 9).
R0344.actuation_evidence: With this prototype, it is possible to vary the shading inside the greenhouse by panel rotation, in relation to the climatic conditions external to the greenhouse.
R0344.justification: Internal radiation at different shading rates is estimated offline from clear-sky calculations and transmittance measured on a physical prototype greenhouse with rotatable PV panels. Nothing describes automated data flow, or panel rotation driven by software, sensors or the model.
